resolved_finding.title: Malformed completed receipts lost preserved native bytes when typed projection failed
evidence: session-daemon-go/internal/grpcapi/operation.go:34-36 maps only ReadStoredOperation failures to gRPC Unavailable.
session-daemon-go/internal/grpcapi/operation.go:38-43 initializes error and status as explicit protobuf null wrappers.
session-daemon-go/internal/grpcapi/operation.go:54-63 marks the known row completed, copies exact legacy bytes, and returns that receipt when typed projection cannot decode the envelope.
session-daemon-go/internal/grpcapi/operation_test.go:336-362 exercises valid untyped and malformed completed rows over authenticated TCP.
session-daemon-go/internal/grpcapi/operation_test.go:399-405 separately proves a closed durable store is gRPC Unavailable with no receipt.

A private scratch-only authenticated TCP regression additionally passed for object-plus-trailing-data, array, string, and JSON-null top-level receipts; every case preserved exact bytes, remained COMPLETED, left typed_response unset, and returned explicit null error/status.

verified_behaviors: Malformed completed receipt bytes are returned unchanged and do not become a transport error.
Trailing-data and non-object completed receipt bytes are returned unchanged without a synthetic typed receipt.
Typed/status projection remains optional; unprojectable rows leave typed_response unset and status/error explicitly null.
A real durable storage read failure remains gRPC Unavailable.
Unknown protobuf identity fields are rejected at request, key, and nullable scope-wrapper levels.
Absent and explicit-null legacy scope values retain null semantics; explicit empty string remains distinct.
Missing, uncertain, and completed rows retain their separate states.
Operation lookup is read-only and does not dispatch or redispatch native runtime work, including after reopen.
The default server registers and advertises exactly DaemonControl, EventStream, and OperationQuery, with operation_lookup=true.
OperationQuery requires bearer authentication over the actual TCP gRPC server.
